title: Deformable Clay Pottery Wheel Sculpting
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D pottery wheel sculpting simulation using Three.js (CDN). The scene simulates a deformable clay body on a spinning pottery wheel where the user sculpts by applying radial and vertical forces.

## Scene Setup
- Background color: #1a1a2e. Add a subtle ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and a warm point light (0xffcc88, intensity 1.2) positioned at (3, 5, 3), plus a fill directional light (0x8888cc, intensity 0.3) from (-2, 3, -1).
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0, 4, 6) looking at origin. OrbitControls enabled but limited: minDistance=3, maxDistance=12, maxPolarAngle=Math.PI/2+0.1.
- A circular pottery wheel base: cylinder geometry (radius 1.5, height 0.15), dark wood material (0x3d2b1f), positioned at y=0. The wheel should visually rotate when spinning.

## Clay Body (Soft Body)
- The clay is represented as a lathe geometry (radial segments: 32, height segments: 16) forming a cylindrical pot shape. Initial shape: a cylinder of radius 0.6, height 2.0, centered on the wheel.
- Store the clay profile as an array of 17 control points (one per height segment + 1), each having {radius, y} where y ranges from 0 to 2.0. Initial radius for all points = 0.6.
- Clay material: MeshStandardMaterial, color 0xc4713b, roughness 0.85, metalness 0.05.
- Rebuild the lathe geometry each frame from the control points when shape changes.
- Track total clay volume using the sum of π * r² * Δy for each segment. Initial volume must be preserved (conservation of mass). When a point's radius decreases, redistribute the lost volume to adjacent points proportionally.

## Pottery Wheel Mechanics
- The wheel has a spin speed (RPM) controllable via a slider (#speed-slider, range 0-120, default 60).
- Display current RPM in a HUD element (#rpm-display).
- The wheel can be started/stopped with a button (#wheel-toggle). When stopped, RPM = 0. When started, it ramps to the slider value over 0.5 seconds.
- The clay mesh should rotate with the wheel (visual rotation only; the profile is axially symmetric).

## Sculpting Interactions
- Mouse interaction: when the user clicks and drags on the clay, a raycaster determines which height segment is targeted. The sculpting tool applies force to that segment and its neighbors (gaussian falloff, sigma=1.5 segments).
- Left-click drag INWARD (mouse moves left): push clay inward (decrease radius). Minimum radius = 0.08.
- Left-click drag OUTWARD (mouse moves right): pull clay outward (increase radius). Maximum radius = 1.4.
- The sculpting force magnitude = mouse delta pixels * 0.003 * (wheelRPM / 60). Sculpting only works when wheel is spinning (RPM > 0).
- Keyboard 'R' resets the clay to the initial cylinder shape.
- Keyboard 'U' undoes the last sculpting stroke (store up to 20 undo snapshots). A stroke is captured on mousedown and committed on mouseup.
- Keyboard 'Y' redoes the last undone stroke.
- Keyboard '1' applies a preset bowl shape: radius profile = [0.6, 0.58, 0.55, 0.5, 0.42, 0.35, 0.3, 0.28, 0.3, 0.38, 0.5, 0.65, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.97, 0.98].
- Keyboard '2' applies a preset vase shape: radius profile = [0.5, 0.55, 0.65, 0.75, 0.8, 0.78, 0.7, 0.55, 0.4, 0.35, 0.32, 0.3, 0.32, 0.38, 0.45, 0.5, 0.52].

## Smoothing
- Keyboard 'S' applies one pass of Laplacian smoothing to the profile: each interior point's radius becomes 0.25*prev + 0.5*self + 0.25*next. First and last points are unchanged.
- Track how many smoothing passes have been applied in total (smoothCount).

## Thickness & Structural Integrity
- Track a wall thickness value for each segment. Initial thickness = 0.15 for all.
- When radius decreases, thickness increases proportionally (clay compressed). When radius increases, thickness decreases.
- If any segment's thickness drops below 0.03, mark the pot as 'cracked'. Display a warning in (#status-display): 'CRACKED!' in red. The cracked state persists until reset.

## HUD / DOM Elements
- Top-left panel with: #rpm-display (text showing RPM), #volume-display (current volume, 2 decimal places), #status-display (shows 'OK' or 'CRACKED!'), #smooth-count (number of smoothing passes), #undo-count (number of available undos), #redo-count (number of available redos).
- #speed-slider: range input for RPM.
- #wheel-toggle: button text toggles between 'Start' and 'Stop'.
- #reset-btn: button that resets clay (same as 'R').

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__ and update every frame:
- wheelRPM: current RPM (number)
- wheelSpinning: boolean
- controlPoints: array of 17 objects {radius, y}
- currentVolume: number (computed volume)
- initialVolume: number (volume at start)
- volumeError: Math.abs(currentVolume - initialVolume) / initialVolume (fractional error)
- minRadius: minimum radius across all control points
- maxRadius: maximum radius across all control points
- cracked: boolean
- minThickness: minimum thickness across all segments
- thicknesses: array of 17 thickness values
- smoothCount: number of smoothing passes applied
- undoStackSize: number of undo snapshots available
- redoStackSize: number of redo snapshots available
- activePreset: null | 'bowl' | 'vase' | 'cylinder'
- sculptingActive: boolean (true while mouse is down on clay)
- meshVertexCount: number of vertices in the clay mesh
- frameCount: number incremented each animation frame
physics_constraints: Conservation of clay volume: when any control point radius changes, total volume (sum of π*r²*Δy per segment) must remain within 1% of initial volume. Minimum radius 0.08, maximum radius 1.4. Wall thickness minimum 0.03 triggers cracking. Sculpting force scales linearly with wheel RPM. Laplacian smoothing uses weights 0.25/0.5/0.25. Undo/redo must perfectly restore previous states.
